controls.title: Prompt Injection
controls.description: Untrusted input alters model behaviour, whether supplied directly by a user or indirectly through retrieved/tool content. The #1 AI attack pattern and requires no authentication.
controls.remediation: Separate instructions from data with SecureContextBuilder; screen inputs with PromptGuardrail; assume injection can succeed and limit blast radius.

controls.title: Sensitive Information Disclosure
controls.description: The model or system leaks PII, secrets, or proprietary data through outputs, logs, reasoning channels, or side channels.
controls.remediation: Scan and redact input and output with DLPScanner; route calls through a gateway; never log raw text.

controls.title: Excessive Agency
controls.description: An agent has more capability, autonomy, or permission than the task needs, so a single manipulated instruction can cause outsized or irreversible damage.
controls.remediation: Apply least privilege with AgentSecurityWrapper: deny-by-default tool allowlist, HITL on irreversible actions, call budgets, kill switch, and the Rule of Two.

controls.title: Supply Chain
controls.description: Compromised or unvetted models, datasets, plugins, tool packages, or dependencies introduce vulnerabilities into the AI system.
controls.remediation: Pin dependencies to exact versions; verify signatures/provenance; maintain an AIBOM/AgBOM; scan dependencies in CI.

controls.title: Data and Model Poisoning
controls.description: Adversarial manipulation of training, fine-tuning, or embedding data corrupts model behaviour or embeds backdoors.
controls.remediation: Curate and review training data; validate and attribute sources; test for memorization on fine-tuned models.

controls.title: Unbounded Consumption
controls.description: Uncontrolled resource use — tokens, cost, recursion, tool calls — enabling denial of wallet/service.
controls.remediation: Set max_tokens and per-user rate limits; cap agent call budgets and recursion depth.

controls.title: Misinformation
controls.description: The model produces confident but incorrect or misleading output that downstream systems or people act on.
controls.remediation: Validate model output against application logic; require citations/grounding; keep a human in the loop for high-stakes decisions.

controls.title: Hidden Context Exposure
controls.description: System prompts, tool schemas, permissions, or other hidden context are disclosed, expanding the attacker's map of the system.
controls.remediation: Never return system prompt content in responses; treat internal context as sensitive.

controls.title: Vector and Embedding Weaknesses
controls.description: Flaws in embeddings and vector stores enable cross-user data bleed, poisoning, or inversion attacks.
controls.remediation: Enforce per-user access filters on every retrieval; authenticate and authorize the vector store; validate memory writes.

controls.title: Improper Output Handling
controls.description: Model output is passed downstream (HTML, SQL, shell, code) without validation, enabling XSS, SQLi, SSRF, or RCE.
controls.remediation: Sanitize output with OutputGuardrail; validate any generated SQL/code against an allowlist; never execute model output directly.
